I’m 65 now, so I don’t chase fancy new things. I farm the way that keeps the land steady and the household safe. On my 20 mu, I will keep most of the land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the most reliable here in Quzhou, and I know how it performs with my well water. I’ll leave a smaller piece for chrysanthemum, because it can bring in cash, but it needs more hand work and more watching, so I cannot put too much area into it with some people working off-farm. My plan is 14 mu in wheat-maize rotation and 6 mu in chrysanthemum.

For wheat, I will sow in early October after simple rotary tillage, using a local improved variety that most people around here trust. I usually put most of the fertilizer down before sowing, then add some urea at jointing if the color is not enough. Wheat is worth feeding because if I save too much on fertilizer and it turns yellow, yield drops fast. But I also won’t push too hard because irrigation and fertilizer both cost money. For maize after wheat, the window is tight, so I will not do heavy tillage. I’ll harvest wheat and plant maize right away with simple land preparation or direct seeding if I can arrange it. Maize needs enough base fertilizer and one topdress around the big bell stage. For chrysanthemum, I will keep the area modest, use more careful hand management, and give fertilizer in 2 or 3 small doses instead of one heavy shot. That crop brings money, but if labor is short or disease comes, it can be troublesome, so I won’t expand it this year.
